commitResults.messageTitle: Correct the expected result of the x/value add test
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide's "Adding a student" manual test expects
`add ... l/Secondary 3 x/value` to report `x/` as an unknown parameter
and leave the roster unchanged. The command instead adds the student
with level `Secondary 3 x/value`, which is the behaviour the User Guide
documents for prefix-like text after a value.

A tester following the DG would report a false failure.

Let's split the step in two and give the x/value command the result it
actually produces.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report wrong-case command words with the lowercase rule
commitResults.messageBody:
A command word typed in the wrong case, such as `NOTE` or `Delete`, is
reported as `Unknown command`, the same error as a misspelling such as
`veiw`.

The user typed a real command and only needs to change its case, so
listing every available command does not tell them what went wrong.

Let's report `Command words must be typed in lowercase. Did you mean
note?` when the word names a command once case is ignored, and keep
the unknown-command error for other words.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report a wrong-case edit note target with the lowercase rule
commitResults.messageBody:
`edit NOTE 1 1 nt/x` reports `INDEX must be a positive whole number`
because `NOTE` is too far from `note` to count as a typo, so the input
goes to the student edit parser. `edit Note 1 1 nt/x` reports `Unknown
edit target`, as if the word were misspelled.

Both inputs name the right target in the wrong case, which the error
should say, in the same way as for a wrong-case `/confirm`.

Let's report `note must be typed in lowercase.` with the `edit note`
format whenever the target equals `note` ignoring case, and keep the
suggestion for real typos such as `notes`.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report a wrong-case delete note target with the lowercase rule
commitResults.messageBody:
`delete NOTE 1 1` reports `delete takes only one INDEX.` because `NOTE`
is too far from `note` to count as a typo and is read as a student
index. `delete Note 1 1` reports `Unknown delete target`, as if the
word were misspelled.

Both inputs name the right target in the wrong case, which the error
should say, as it already does for a wrong-case `/confirm`.

Let's report `note must be typed in lowercase.` with the `delete note`
format whenever the first word equals `note` ignoring case, and keep
the suggestion for real typos such as `notes`.

commitResults.messageTitle: Bring the UI docs in line with the profile panel

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject non-typo words early in isMistypedTarget
commitResults.messageBody:
ParserUtil#isMistypedTarget returns one four-term boolean expression,
so a reader must evaluate every term to see which words count as a
typo. It also computes the edit distance for words it will reject.

Let's return early for empty, exact, and parameter-like words, leaving
the distance check as the final step, and add direct tests for each
partition of the word and for the boundary between 2 and 3 edits.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract the overlap length of two screen ranges
commitResults.messageBody:
ScreenBoundsCalculator#calculateIntersectionArea computes each side of
the overlap with a nested max/min expression repeated for both axes,
which hides that both lines do the same calculation.

Let's extract calculateOverlapLength and add tests for partial
overlap on both axes, full containment, and overlap on one axis only.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clamp the profile scroll value with Math.clamp
commitResults.messageBody:
StudentProfilePanel#scrollProfilePane limits the new scroll value with
nested Math.max and Math.min calls, which take a moment to read as a
clamp.

Let's use Math.clamp, which says the intent directly. The pane's vmin
and vmax are never changed from their defaults, so the range is never
empty and the result is unchanged. A new test pages past both ends of
the pane and checks that the value stays within its range.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject data files with content after the JSON value
commitResults.messageBody:
JsonUtil reads the first JSON value in a file and ignores anything after
it, so a data file holding two documents loads without any warning.

The next save then overwrites the file, which permanently discards the
ignored records without creating a backup.

Let's reject any content other than whitespace after the first value,
so the existing data-load error and backup apply to these files.

The check is in JsonUtil because the pinned Jackson 2.7 does not have
FAIL_ON_TRAILING_TOKENS, and upgrading would change the established
build configuration. It also applies to preferences.json, which falls
back to the default preferences.

Fixes #320

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep file contents and user paths out of load logs
commitResults.messageBody:
JsonUtil logs the whole exception when a JSON file fails to load, and
Jackson messages quote the text they could not parse. An unquoted value
in a hand-edited data file therefore writes part of a student's details
or lesson note to the log. Absolute paths in load logs also contain the
OS user name.

Logs must not contain personal data, and users may attach log files to
bug reports without checking them.

Let's,
* log the exception type with its line and column instead of the
  exception itself
* log data and preference file paths relative to the home folder
* document both rules in the logging guide

The user-facing load error and the backup behavior do not change.

Fixes #314

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'master' into 311-314-317-320-beta-bug-fixes
Stop rejecting a/ and t/ in student fields
commitResults.messageBody:
The add and edit parsers reject the inherited AddressBook prefixes a/
and t/ wherever they appear, so "n/Raj a/l Kumar" and
"sub/Art t/shirts" fail with an unknown parameter error.

Names may contain slashes, and a/l is a real name particle, so these
commands should work. Other unrecognized prefix-like text already stays
in the value before it.

Let's,
* stop tokenizing a/ and t/, so they behave like other unrecognized text
* remove the legacy prefix check and constants, which are now unused
* update the User Guide, Developer Guide and tests to the new behavior

An unrecognized prefix straight after the edit index is still reported
as an unknown parameter.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge upstream master into 334-show-profile-after-note
Command box: Replace pasted tabs and line breaks with spaces
commitResults.messageBody:
The command box is a JavaFX TextField, which deletes tabs, line
breaks and other control characters from inserted text. A note
pasted over two lines, or with a tab, is saved with the words around
them joined, and the user is not told. The parser never receives
those characters, so its non-printable error, which the User Guide
quotes, cannot appear.

Let's give the text field a TextFormatter that replaces each control
character with a space before the field removes it, counting a
Windows line break (CRLF) as one. When a CRLF shrinks to one space,
the caret and anchor are moved to match, because
TextFormatter.Change#setText leaves them where they were.

Blocking the paste and showing the parser's error was considered,
but it needs a new link from CommandBox to the result display, and
pasting a note written in another app is a reasonable thing to do.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update UG and DG for pasted tabs and line breaks
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide says a note with a tab or line break is rejected with
an error, but the command box now turns each one into a space.

Let's describe the new behaviour in the note and edit note sections
and in the command format notes, replacing the AB3 warning about
pasting from a PDF. Let's also explain the TextFormatter in the
Developer Guide's UI section, and add a paste step to the manual
testing instructions for adding a session note.

commitResults.messageTitle: UI tests: Skip empty clipboard formats when saving
commitResults.messageBody:
The paste tests save the system clipboard and restore it afterwards.
On Linux, the clipboard can list a format whose content is null, and
Clipboard#setContent rejects a null value, so restoring the saved
content throws a NullPointerException and fails the Ubuntu CI build.

Let's leave formats without content out of the saved copy. They
hold no data, so nothing is lost when the clipboard is restored.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report wrong-case nt/ before a later nt/
commitResults.messageBody:
`note 1 NT/a nt/b` reports `Unexpected text before the first
parameter: NT/a.` instead of asking for a lowercase nt/. The
wrong-case check only runs when no lowercase nt/ is found, so a
wrong-case prefix before a lowercase one lands in the preamble and is
reported as stray text.

Let's also check the preamble for a wrong-case nt/ before checking it
for stray text. Only the preamble is checked, so a wrong-case NT/
inside the note text is still saved as text.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test wrong-case nt/ before nt/ without an index
Remove unused removeSessionHistory method
commitResults.messageBody:
Model, ModelManager and AddressBook each define removeSessionHistory,
but no command or other production code calls it. Deleting a student
already removes their session history through removeStudent, so the
method is dead code kept alive only by its own tests.

Unlike every other session-note operation in AddressBook, it also
skips the check that the student is in the roster, which makes it
easy to misuse if someone picks it up later.

Let's delete the method, the tests that existed only to exercise it,
and its entry in the Developer Guide's list of Model operations.
Removing a student's notes stays covered by the removeStudent and
deleteStudent tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tidy session note code to the coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
A code-quality review of the session note code found several small
departures from the SE-EDU Java coding standard and the course's
code-quality guidelines:

* RECORDED_AT_FORMAT also formats and parses lastEditedAt, so its
  name is misleading.
* NoteCommandParser repeats the same withFormat call with the note
  command's format and example five times.
* SessionNote.isInvisible and HomeFolder.isJarFile are non-trivial
  private methods without header comments.
* One @throws tag starts with a lowercase "if", unlike the others.
* Some lines in session note code and tests exceed the 110-character
  soft limit.
* The test name empty_noNotes does not state the expected behavior.

Let's rename the formatter to TIMESTAMP_FORMAT, extract a
withNoteFormat helper, add the missing comments, rewrap the long
lines, and rename the test. Behavior is unchanged, and the existing
tests run every changed line.

commitResults.messageTitle: Improve quality of jiahw4ng-authored code (#350)
commitResults.messageBody:
Three spots had expressions that were harder to read than needed:
a four-term boolean return in isMistypedTarget, the overlap formula
repeated for each axis in calculateIntersectionArea, and nested
Math.max/Math.min calls when clamping the profile scroll value.

Let's return early for each kind of word isMistypedTarget rejects,
so the edit distance is computed only when needed. Let's also
extract the overlap formula into calculateOverlapLength, and use
Math.clamp for the scroll value.

Let's add direct tests for isMistypedTarget, more overlap cases for
findLargestOverlapIndex, and a test that paging past either end of
the profile pane keeps the scroll value in range.

commitResults.messageTitle: [#354] Remove AB3 placeholders from About Us and team pages (#366)
commitResults.messageBody:
The About Us page still showed AB3's contact email and linked to two
placeholder portfolio pages, and the unused John Doe sample page and
image were still in the docs folder.

Let's remove the AB3 email, the placeholder portfolio links and their
stub pages, and the John Doe page and image.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add UI screenshots to the User Guide (#364)
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide's two screenshots were outdated. Ui.png still showed
UTC offsets that the app no longer displays, and helpMessage.png
still showed the AddressBook user guide URL. The guide also had no
screenshots of command results, errors or confirmation prompts.

Let's retake both, and add captioned screenshots of the first launch,
command errors, the result of each command, the session-note
history, the delete previews and confirmations, and the data-file
recovery dialog.

commitResults.messageTitle: [#367] Tighten UG command sections, screenshots and notation (#369)
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide said parameters could be in any order, although
indices come first and /confirm comes last. Most screenshots were
full-window with no set width, several command sections repeated
the generic error messages, and some text used development-history
wording.

Let's state the parameter order rules, order each command section as
purpose, format, rules, examples and display details, and link to
"Fixing command errors" instead of repeating its messages. Let's
also crop the screenshots, give every image a width, drop a
redundant one, and name a/ and t/ as the only rejected prefixes.

commitResults.messageTitle: [#368] Trim DG and add design rationale, UML and Effort appendix (#370)
commitResults.messageBody:
Many Developer Guide implementation sections narrated the code in
long paragraphs, few design decisions explained the alternatives,
the proposed archiving feature had no diagram, and there was no
Effort appendix.

Let's trim and merge those sections into focused bullets, and add
design considerations with pros and cons for stable student IDs,
confirmed deletion and save-failure rollback. Let's also add a
sequence diagram for the proposed archive and restore flow, and an
Effort appendix comparing TutorTrack with AB3.

commitResults.messageTitle: [#338] Audit user stories against the implemented product (#341)
commitResults.messageBody:
The requirements appendix listed sample-data stories for a product
that starts empty, mixed unbuilt features such as find and undo with
implemented ones, marked the implemented note editing as unlikely to
have, and gave a weak benefit for session-note counts.

Let's split the stories into current MVP and future tables, remove
the sample-data stories, promote note editing and add note deletion
as must-haves, and give the note count a concrete benefit.

commitResults.messageTitle: [#311, #314, #317, #320] Fix beta bugs in logs, data and guides (#372)
commitResults.messageBody:
Beta testing found four bugs. The out-of-roster error showed the
index in brackets like a note number, and guide source links still
pointed to AddressBook-Level3. A data file with extra content after
its JSON value loaded without error, so the next save silently
dropped that content. A failed load also logged Jackson's message,
which can quote note text, along with absolute paths that contain
the OS user name.

Let's drop the brackets from the out-of-roster error, point the
source links to this repository, and reject any non-whitespace
content after the first JSON value so the usual data-load error and
backup apply. Let's also log only the exception type, line and
column for a failed load, and show data and preference file paths
relative to the home folder.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor add parsing, startup loading, and phone checks (#373)
commitResults.messageBody:
The add parser repeated its prefix list for the duplicate check and
failed with a bare NoSuchElementException if a verified prefix was
ever missing. initModelManager mixed loading with failure handling,
the phone separator regex was an unnamed literal, and the phone
validation test was one long method.

Let's reuse SUPPORTED_PREFIXES for the duplicate check, throw an
IllegalStateException with context for a broken parser invariant,
and extract loadInitialAddressBook and handleDataLoadingFailure from
initModelManager. Let's also name PHONE_SEPARATOR_REGEX, simplify the
optional email check, and split the phone tests by partition with
boundary cases on each digit limit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Polish About Us roles, links and UG prefix wording (#380)
commitResults.messageBody:
About Us listed Roger as a project advisor, gave two members the
same UI role, and mixed http and https links. The User Guide called
a/ and t/ obsolete AddressBook prefixes, which means nothing to a
user who has never used AddressBook.

Let's give each member an accurate role and responsibilities, use
https for every link, and describe a/ and t/ as unsupported prefixes
that are rejected as unknown parameters.

The About Us photos still need replacing, so #374 stays open.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove "Fixing command errors" from the User Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The section listed every kind of command error with its exact message
text and two screenshots. TutorTrack's error messages already name the
problem and show the correct format with an example, so the section
repeated what users see on screen, and each quoted message was one more
thing that could drift from the app.

Each command section already says what happens when its command is
rejected. Remove the section, its screenshots and the links to it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Simplify the note section of the User Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The note rules listed eleven bullets, most of them exact error messages
or rules the command-format notes already cover, such as lowercase
prefixes and pasted line breaks. The block was hard to scan, and every
quoted message was one more thing that could drift from the app.

Keep only what a user needs to write a valid note and the nt/ rule that
would surprise them. Explain what each example does, and replace the
screenshot with one whose alt text names the student shown and whose
display width does not exceed its real size, so it is not blurred.

commitResults.messageTitle: Simplify the saving section of the User Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The section described saving in prose, including a note about deletion
previews that read like an implementation detail. It also repeated the
data file location, backup steps and write-protected folder behaviour
that "Editing the data file", the FAQ and Known issues already cover.

List which commands change the data and which do not, so users can see
at a glance when TutorTrack saves, and remove the repeated paragraphs.

commitResults.messageTitle: Simplify the data file section of the User Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The section explained the timestamp format, note ordering and other
details that rarely matter to someone editing the file, and its caution
said an empty roster replaces the file even though any roster created
before the fix would do so. It also said note text may contain no tabs
or line breaks, although those at the start or end are trimmed on load.

Keep the rules a user is likely to break when editing the file, add the
rule that lastEditedAt cannot be earlier than recordedAt, and state when
tabs and line breaks are trimmed or rejected.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge remote-tracking branch 'upstream/master' into fixing-user-guide-issues
commitResults.messageBody:
# Conflicts:
#	docs/UserGuide.md

commitResults.messageTitle: [#381] Clarify how CommandBox delegates command execution (#382)
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide said CommandBox delegates execution to Logic,
while the UI class diagram connects only MainWindow to Logic, which
left the callback path unclear.

Let's explain that CommandBox records each non-blank submission and
then passes it to a CommandExecutor supplied by MainWindow, which
delegates execution to Logic.

commitResults.messageTitle: Stop rejecting a/ and t/ in student fields and tidy the guides (#386)
commitResults.messageBody:
The add and edit parsers rejected the inherited AddressBook prefixes
a/ and t/ wherever they appeared, so valid input such as the name
Raj a/l Kumar failed with an unknown-parameter error. Several manual
tests in the Developer Guide could not be followed as written, and
the User Guide told users to recall a failed command that was still
in the command box.

Let's treat a/ and t/ like any other unrecognized prefix-like text,
keeping them in the value before them, and remove the legacy prefix
check. Let's also fix the guides' failed-command advice, the command
history and write-protected folder manual tests, and some stale
wording.

commitResults.messageTitle: [#337] Simplify the session-note deletion sequence diagram (#383)
commitResults.messageBody:
The session-note deletion sequence diagram combined preview,
confirmation, persistence and profile refresh in one large diagram,
which hid the core flow.

Let's replace it with two activity diagrams, one for the preview and
one for the next command, covering cancellation, failed confirmation
and save-failure rollback, and update the Developer Guide to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: [#384] Align the Logic overview with the add-command example (#385)
commitResults.messageBody:
The architecture sequence diagram shows a successful add, but the
Logic overview beside it walked through deletion preview and
confirmation, so readers could not connect the two.

Let's explain the Logic classes using the add command, name
AddCommand in the Logic class diagram, and narrow the parser class
diagram to the classes used to parse add. Detailed add and deletion
flows stay in their own sections.
